headline: High-risk shared write and API surfaces create default conflict and cascading-error exposure; prompt-injection and compliance risks are moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest files, browser content, and MCP outputs, while semantica can read web pages, files, and MCP resources. That creates a plausible default instruction-injection path if semantica processes attacker-controlled content and Devin later treats it as trusted. The shared channel is indirect, so this is below high.
conditions: IF semantica ingests untrusted web/file/MCP content and emits it into shared artifacts
IF Devin reads those artifacts as instructions without provenance filtering
mitigations: Restrict both agents to provenance-tagged inputs only
Disable MCP bridges between the two agents for untrusted sources
Add a manual review step before Devin acts on semantica-produced text
Use separate workspaces for each agent
requires-engineering: enforce content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch sensitive enterprise artifacts: Devin handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets; semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and private keys. Their shared file and API surfaces make cross-exposure plausible in default workflows, though the profiles do not prove a single shared workspace or uncontrolled third-party upload path.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository, document set, or data lake
IF either agent is allowed to sync its working context into shared integrations or APIs
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces
Remove secrets from shared folders before either agent runs
Limit each agent to least-privilege credentials
Audit outbound API destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss-prevention and redaction controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write files, modify git state, install packages, and spawn subprocesses. Devin explicitly supports parallel sessions with shared integrations, and semantica uses a shared intelligence layer across agents. Without locking, concurrent writes to the same repo or mutable resource can corrupt state or overwrite each other, matching the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or filesystem path
IF either agent performs writes while the other is active without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint repos or directories
Serialize write phases with a simple lock file
Pause one agent before the other edits shared state
Use branch-per-agent workflows
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control and conflict detection

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that acts inside its workspace, and semantica emphasizes provenance, decision records, and deterministic graph construction. If semantica’s outputs are fed into Devin without verification, Devin can act on incorrect facts and propagate them into code, tickets, or Slack. The pair lacks an explicit verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF semantica outputs are used as authoritative inputs to Devin
IF Devin is permitted to execute changes or send messages based on those outputs without human review
mitigations: Require human approval before Devin acts on semantica outputs
Add a verification checklist for facts and citations
Keep semantica outputs read-only until reviewed
Log provenance for every downstream action
requires-engineering: implement automated cross-checking between graph facts and source documents

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, docs, and integration tokens, while semantica handles enterprise data, contracts, audit trails, and private keys. The profiles show broad data classes and cloud/API handling, but no explicit residency or certification mismatch. The safest reading is a medium compliance risk from mixed retention and access controls, not a proven breach.
conditions: IF regulated or contract-restricted data is routed through both agents
IF their logging or retention settings differ for the same data class
mitigations: Classify data before routing it to either agent
Keep regulated data out of shared integrations
Review retention settings for both tools
Restrict access to private keys and tokens
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion workflows
